o1.biggest_strength: It goes all in on what the pilot says works: controllers, sent within 60 days of a pricing-page change, no links, the 9-to-4 proof written as a sentence, and an honest 6.8% to 7.9% reply target that doesn't multiply untested gains.
o1.biggest_mistake: Holding most of the 1,900 controllers on a watch list until their pricing page changes could leave a lot of my best segment unsent for months, and the plan never sizes how many will actually get flagged.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Estimate how many of the 1,900 get flagged per week, add a fallback opener for the rest, and add the opt-out footer and the suppression rules (current customers, open opportunities).

o2.biggest_strength: A complete, runnable playbook: the right segment, trigger-first send order with a fallback opener for unflagged contacts, an opt-out footer, suppression rules, and pilot-based expectations with the arithmetic shown.
o2.biggest_mistake: Loading unflagged controllers with a pain-statement opener mixes in a weaker version the pilot never tested for this role, and step 2's meeting ask comes early for cold finance leads.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Show the expected rates for the flagged and unflagged groups separately, and make step 2's ask lighter than a 20-minute meeting.

reason: Both pick the right people, the right moment and no links. The second one I could hand to my reps tomorrow because it has a send order, fallbacks, an opt-out footer and exclusions, while the first could leave most of my best list idle.
